Florida State Seminoles Louisville Cardinals NCAAF Louisville looks to get back on track following a second straight loss in ACC play when it hosts Florida State at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium tonight at 7 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Cardinals are 4.5-point home favorites, but my Florida State vs. Louisville predictions and college football picks for Friday, Oct. 9 expect the Seminoles' offense to take advantage of one of the country's worst defenses. Who will win Florida State vs Louisville: Florida State +4.5 Florida State is coming off a narrative-changing victory after beating Virginia by 31 points. The Seminoles have now covered in each of their last two games against FBS opponents, showcasing one of the country's best run games. With Ashton Daniels at QB and Ousmane Kromah at running back, FSU is 12th nationally in EPA per rush and 17th in rush success rate (49.7%). That could be a problem for a Louisville defense that's been one of the worst in the Power Four, allowing the 14th-most yards per game in the country (423). Daniels and Kromah have combined for 755 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns in five games, and if they get going on the ground, Florida State can turn this into a shootout on the road. I like FSU at +3.5 or better . TOP PICK Florida State vs Louisville Over/Under pick: Over 59.5 Louisville has an offense that looks capable of winning the ACC and a defense that looks capable of losing every game against a quality opponent. In four FBS games, Louisville has averaged 33.5 points per game and allowed 33.2 ppg. The Cardinals have hit the Over in three of those games, and I like them to do it again with a total of 60.5 or better . With Lincoln Kienholz expected to be healthy for Louisville, he should keep the offense humming. The Cardinals rank top 25 nationally in offensive success rate (49.7%) , and Kienholz has accounted for 15 touchdowns and a 77.2 QBR. Kienholz, along with running back Isaac Brown (and Keyjuan Brown if he plays), should push a Florida State defense that's 98th in rush success rate (46.9%) and 93rd in net adjusted EPA per play. Florida State vs Louisville combo Louisville's defense is the reason it's already lost three games this season and why it's failed to cover in two straight ACC matchups. Louisville doesn't create negative plays on defense, ranking third-last in the ACC in havoc rate (13.2%) and 88th in net EPA per play. With Kromah and Daniels carrying FSU's ground attack, they will be able to break loose for big plays and approach 30+ points. Meanwhile, FSU has defensive issues of its own, ranking 92nd in available yards percentage (52.1%) . A high-scoring game should lead to a back-and-forth final frame. Florida State +4.5 Florida State vs Louisville prop: Florida State team total Over 27.5 Florida State has scored 28+ points in four of five games this season, and Louisville has allowed 28+ points to all four of its FBS opponents this season. I'd play the Over on the Seminoles' team total at 27.5 or better . The Seminoles are averaging 33.2 ppg this season, and Kromah has quickly become one of the best running backs in the country. He ranks top 10 nationally in forced missed tackles on runs (28) and runs of 10+ yards (14). Daniels' mobility has opened up the offense, too, with the Auburn transfer sitting top 25 in the country in QBR (80.5) thanks to the damage he's doing on the ground. A 30-27 loss to Wake Forest and a 31-28 loss to NC State later, and now the Cardinals have to win to stay alive in the ACC race. Florida State was done. Head coach Mike Norvell was all but fired, and then everything flipped. The Seminoles tuned up against Central Arkansas, and then stunned Virginia 38-7. Win this, and the season narrative totally changes. Florida State vs Louisville Quick Hits Florida State is on the road for four games in the next five, with a trip to Miami up next before hosting Clemson. The defense pitched one of its best games in a long time, considering the circumstances, holding the Cavalier passing game in check with a monstrous day from the pass rush. The Noles generated ten sacks and 12 tackles for loss. The relentless pressure should continue against a Louisville offensive front that's having a problem keeping teams out of the backfield. Why Louisville Will Win Can Florida State show up on the road? It's not quite fair to dog the Noles for losing at Alabama, but the program has lost 13 straight games outside of Tallahassee, going back to the win over Florida late in 2023. Louisville has to take a deep breath after the NC State loss. It played well. The ground game was great, quarterback Lincoln Kienholz was fine on his dinged up ankle, and everything was fine outside of three lost fumbles. Florida State hasn't forced a takeaway in a month. Florida State vs Louisville Prediction, Betting Lines Florida State isn't awful. The pieces are there – the ground game is solid, and look out if that pass rush keeps on rolling – but they have a hard time always fitting together. The Seminoles will crank up plenty of yards and points – the Louisville defense isn't anything special – but the offense will stall a few too many times, and the Cardinals will find their offensive scoring punch after two straight disappointments. away.headline: Louisville's initial week 6 injury report reveals a key advantage for Florida State on defense
away.blurb: After pulling off a win over Virginia in Week 5 with plenty of injuries , Florida State will need to do it all over again with Louisville looming this weekend. The first Week 6 injury report has already been made available, and even at full strength, the Seminoles will be entering the game with a number of players banged up. Playing through injuries and adapting quickly can be tough, but Louisville will have to do the same thing, and Florida State needs to take advantage. The Cardinals have a handful of players who have already been ruled out for the game, and that part of the injury report has mainly stayed the same over the past few weeks. There are a few new additions to the report that could be important, including starting offensive lineman Cason Henry. Henry, who is listed as questionable for the game, is a starting tackle for Louisville who has been a key part of the run game for the Cardinals. Florida State improved as a unit defensively against Virginia, but the team still struggles in a few areas. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska is getting ready for a huge Big Ten matchup against Indiana, and Adam Carriker breaks down what the Huskers have to do if they want to pull off the upset and earn some serious respect. This is one of those games that can change the way people look at a team. Nebraska has put together a strong start, but now the Huskers get a chance to prove it against a ranked Indiana team led by Curt Cignetti. Indiana has been one of the best teams in the Big Ten, and this game will give Matt Rhule’s team a chance to show how far it has come. Carriker starts by looking back at the history between Nebraska and Indiana; he then shifts to Nebraska’s offense and quarterback Anthony Colandrea. If Nebraska is going to win this game, Colandrea will need to have a big day. He has to make smart decisions, take care of the football, and make plays with both his arm and his legs. Carriker also compares Colandrea to Indiana’s quarterback Josh Hoover and talks about why Nebraska needs to put pressure on Hoover and force him into mistakes. The Huskers’ pass catchers are another major part of the matchup. Nebraska has playmakers who can make a difference, and Carriker takes a closer look at players like Kwazi Gilmer and how they match up with Indiana’s defense. On the other side of the ball, Nebraska’s defense could be one of the biggest factors in the game. Rob Aurich and the Nebraska defense will need to be at their best, especially on third down. Indiana has talented receivers, solid running backs, and an offense that can hurt teams in several different ways. Nebraska cannot afford to give up easy conversions or big plays. One of the biggest topics in the episode is penalties. Nebraska had 16 penalties last week while Indiana had zero. That is a massive difference, and Carriker makes it clear that Nebraska cannot expect to beat a ranked team if it keeps hurting itself. Cleaning up the penalties is one of his biggest keys to the game. Carriker wraps up the show by laying out five keys for Nebraska: limit penalties, stop the run, play four full quarters, run the football, and limit big plays. None of those things are complicated, but Nebraska has to do all five if it wants to compete and win. The Huskers also need to be ready for a physical game. Carriker talks about trading blows with Indiana and matching the Hoosiers for all four quarters. This cannot be a game where Nebraska plays well for two or three quarters and then fades late. The second half will be huge. Carriker also throws in a little extra motivation with a beard bet if Nebraska wins. At the end of the show, he gives his final score prediction: Indiana 27, Nebraska 24. He sees it as a close game, but Nebraska will need a big performance from Colandrea, a strong game from the defense, and much cleaner football to pull off the upset. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! picks.headline: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Indiana
picks.blurb: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Indiana - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Bills stun Rams in OT WNBA Finals arena debacle Brewers beat Dodgers again Guardians win ALCS Game 1 Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Indiana Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's midterms for Nebraska football following its best start since 2016. Now, the Huskers welcome Indiana to Lincoln for arguably the biggest game of the season for both teams. For Nebraska, it'll either finally get over the hump and snap its 30-game losing streak against ranked opponents or start another dreadful latter half of the season. For Indiana, it's either another win or its first loss since 2024. Though this is a matchup between two undefeated teams, the contrast is present. The Hoosiers are the defending national champions, while the Huskers still have yet to prove themselves. But other factors differentiate these teams, despite their many similarities. Though both teams have slow starts offensively, Indiana has been able to march downfield early in games, only to fall short in the red zone. For Nebraska, its early-game struggles come down to the offensive line needing time to find its footing. The Hoosiers can surely exploit that, considering they held Northwestern to 32 rushing yards on 27 carries. Now Indiana can swallow up the run again for Nebraska, whose top runner in the past two weeks has been Anthony Colandrea. The Hoosiers also got to Aiden Chiles four times, who is capable of taking off. Colandrea took two sacks against Maryland, so either he's going to be taking off or he's going to be tasting the turf a lot more against the Hoosiers. But if there is time in the pocket, Colandrea can make things happen. Indiana did allow Chiles to throw 22-of-29 for 293 yards, so Colandrea could put up similar numbers. But Colandrea isn't flawless in the air. Though he's thrown only one true interception, Colandrea has been off target at times. Josh Hoover's in a similar boat but has been clean through five games, with no interceptions. Now, with reports of winds being at 17 miles per hour come kickoff, both quarterbacks could be limited in the air. However, Hoover has been sacked six times in the last four games and has only 18 rushing yards. If the Blackshirts can pressure him, they can at least slow Indiana's passing game further. That only leaves Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr. for Nebraska. The duo combined for 1,107 rushing yards on 152 carries, averaging 7.3 per carry. That is a problem for the Huskers. They allowed a few big runs against Maryland and nearly 150 total yards. So, the Hoosiers can either deliver devastating blows or just chip away at the clock to get to Nebraska's defense. But that only looks at the team's execution on plays, and there are more factors to consider. The Huskers enter the game with 43 penalties after drawing 16 last week. Though there was some controversy regarding that game, 16 penalties in a game don't just happen. Nebraska has allowed teams to continue drives due to penalties or has ended its own drives due to penalties. Indiana has only gotten 17 on the season, so that's another area the Huskers can exploit. Overall, Nebraska has multiple ways to come out on top here. If the Huskers can get the run game going and shut down Indiana's, there's a chance. But the line's struggles and penalties take away some of their advantages. Plus, with that recent history and its current issues, Nebraska needs to truly take that next step if it wants to win. But that won't happen unless it comes out like a championship-caliber team, or the Hoosiers play their worst game of the season. But this game will feel like last year's Michigan game. Indiana won't blow out the Huskers like in 2024, but it will still get the win. Norton Sat, October 10, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Indiana football is set for its second road matchup of the 2026 season, facing Nebraska on Saturday afternoon in Lincoln. Both teams enter the matchup undefeated at 5-0 and 2-0 in conference play. Ordinarily a record like that would likely result in an AP top-25 ranking for the Cornhuskers but basically nothing makes sense anymore and you've just kinda gotta roll with it. Here's three bold predictions for the matchup: Lee Beebe Jr. proves critical Indiana's new-look running game has left shredded defenses in its wake a both Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr. have looked excellent on the ground early on. Richard is absolutely the Hoosiers' lead back and deserves the honors that come with it, but Beebe Jr.'s role has proven critical, specifically against Northwestern. He looked great against Rutgers as well despite carrying an availability report injury designation into the game. He'll prove just as crucial against a Nebraska team that's had a tough go of defending the run at times. Richard looks like the Big Ten's best running back, but Beebe's carries being productive will make this one of the most fearsome backfields in the country. Anthony Colandrea tests Indiana's linebacker corps The last mobile quarterback Indiana faced was Northwestern's Aidan Chiles and that didn't go entirely well for the Hoosier defense. Indiana was able to limit Chiles and the Chip Kelly-led Northwestern offense more than most, for sure, but his escapability at the position was a tough task for Indiana's defensive line to generate the kind of pressure that leads to bad throws. More often, he was able to buy time with his legs to open up some passing opportunities downfield. Anthony Colandrea, Nebraska's quarterback, is also mobile and has punished defenses on the ground with his legs more than Chiles this year. This is the kind of situation where you're glad Indiana has seen a similar sort of player before and has film to correct what can be corrected. That said, while Indiana's defensive line is monstrous and its linebackers consistently make plays at the second level, I think Colandrea realllly tests the latter unit. Indiana's linebackers aren't necessarily built to contain mobile quarterbacks from a pure athletic standpoint, moreso to help run the defense and fly in from the second level. Are there ways of scheming around that? Yes. Does Indiana have perhaps the best schemer in the country running its defense? Also yes. Either way, this is something to watch for. Charlie Becker's biggest play isn't a catch Charlie Becker is known nationally for his incredible play out wide, hauling in just about any ball sent his way for huge gains time and again. More locally, he's also known for his ferocity in the run game. There just aren't a ton of receivers with Becker's size, strength and mindset as a run blocker. He treats it just as seriously as his role as a pass catcher, which was a huge asset to Indiana's offense last year and remains so this year. He'll be doing more downfield with a more explosive running game. Look for a highlight-reel style block from Becker here. Join the conversation! away.headline: Riley Van Poppel injury threatens Nebraska where Indiana can hurt it most
away.blurb: Considering that Van Poppel looked like he wasn't adjusting all that well to Aurich's defense in fall camp and then surged into a situation where he was getting as many snaps as any defensive lineman in the last few weeks, it couldn't be a worse time for an injury to keep him out of Saturday morning's massive game. The good for Nebraska heading into the massive showdown against Indiana on Saturday is that the team is mostly healthy. Jamal Rule, Jacory Barney, and Mekhi Nelson are off the injury reports entirely. The bad news is that Thursday night's report added a defensive player the Huskers can scarcely afford to miss. Riley Van Poppel's apparent injury isn't a big deal simply because he's a defensive lineman, and the Hoosiers' run game is easily the best the Huskers have faced so far this year. His potential absence is also a big issue because Van Poppel's playing time has increased as the season has gone on. Van Poppel's use by Nebraska defensive coordinator Rob Aurich has, in fact, never been bigger than it has been since Nebraska started Big Ten play. Against Ohio, he saw just 30 snaps. Against Bowling Green, it was down to 18, and he had just 28 snaps against North Dakota. However, he tallied 46 snaps against Michigan State and 44last week against Maryland. Riley Van Poppel injury could weaken Nebraska football front against Indiana running backs Van Poppel hasn't always been on the stat sheet. He has just 7 tackles, but 2 of those were sacks. He's also got 9 quarterback pressures, including 5 in Big Ten games alone. While his 2 sacks came in non-conference play, he's shown he can make an impact in the trenches, with 2 quarterback hurries and a quarterback hit against the Spartans and 2 more hurries against the Terrapins. "I think I'm playing probably the best I have in four years right now," Van Poppel said after Nebraska's Week 4 win over Michigan State . Van Poppel has also been a vocal leader for Nebraska, especially after earning a single-digit jersey last year and being given the option of keeping it this fall. Instead of once again wearing No. 5, he went back to his No. 44, saying he didn't believe he lived up to his own standard of what a player wearing a single digit jersey should be like. “He (Rhule) gave me the option to keep one, but I don’t see it that way. I want the guys who were truly voted to be the single digits, and if I need to go back to a different number, at the end of the day, it’s a number.” As is the policy with the Big Ten Availability Reports, it's not a guarantee that Riley Van Poppel will miss Nebraska's biggest game of the year. The Huskers will release two more before game time. One report will update the status of injured players on Friday night, and another two hours before kickoff. away.source: Hoosier State of Mind on MSN
away.blurb: The biggest bit of good news from this week's initial availability report is that cornerback AJ Harris is not featured. Harris, a transfer from Penn State, went down in Week 1 against North Texas and hasn't been able to return to the field since. Harris has 35 appearances with 27 starts under his belt after one season at Georgia and two at Penn State. He came to Bloomington after an impressive junior season that saw him earn All-Big Ten defensive honorable mention recognition with the Nittany Lions in 2025. Jaylen Bell has played well in Harris' absence, but it seems that Harris now full-go for Week 6. Defensive lineman Daniel Ndukwe is also off this week's availability report after missing Week 5 against Rutgers. His return brings even more depth and talent to Indiana's dangerous defensive front. The lone Hoosier RB still sidelined is Khobie Martin, which doesn't come as a surprise as he continues to nurse a broken forearm that he suffered in Week 1. WR Lebron Bond has also been upgraded to questionable for Saturday's matchup against Rutgers. The absences of Martin and Williams are expected, leaving the Hoosiers with few injury surprises at this time. The lone downside is Andrew Barker being ruled out. He was injured against Rutgers and won't be able suit up for the Nebraska game. All things considered, this initial Week 6 injury report brings plenty of good news for the Hoosiers. Five players have been ruled out for Week 6 for the Cornhuskers: WR Larry Miles, DB Kahmir Prescott, LB Jase Reynolds, LB Jacob Bower, and DL Gabe Moore. Two other Cornhuskers, TE Carter Nelson and LB Gage Stenger are listed as doubtful. Kick-off betwen Indiana and Nebraska is set for Noon ET on Saturday afternoon. The Indiana Hoosiers have been dealing with some key injuries throughout the past couple of weeks. But even with some reliable contributors sidelined, Indiana has been able to cruise to a 5-0 record to start the season. However, the competition is about to increase substantially the rest of the way. The Hoosiers travel to Lincoln to take on undefeated Nebraska in Week 6, and with matchups against Ohio State, Michigan, USC, and Washington still looming, getting as healthy as possible is of the utmost importance for Curt Cignetti and company. It is more notable who is not on the report as IU looks to get cornerback AJ Harris back after the starting corner was injured just seven snaps into the season. For Nebraska it looks like freshman running back Jamal Rule will be back this week and Jacory Barney will be a full go after being a game time decision last week. The Thursday update had no changes for Indiana, but there were some for Nebraska. picks.blurb: Arizona Wildcats football at West Virginia Mountaineers score predictions | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 13, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football Rich Rodriguez was Arizona’s coach from 2012-17, during which time he went 43-35 and reached bowl games in five of six seasons. Since parting ways with RichRod, the Wildcats have gone 42-54 and played in two bowl games, those coming in the last three seasons. When Arizona (4-1, 1-1 Big 12) takes on West Virginia (3-2, 0-2) on Saturday morning it will mark the first time since 1992 it is facing a former head coach. The UA went 2-4 against Larry Smith , their coach from 1980-86, while he was at USC. How will the Wildcats do on the road against their former coach? Our staff makes its predictions. Kim Doss — Arizona wins 35-31 It’s a tale of two dramatically different offenses. Arizona has the highest pass completion percentage (72.6) in the Big 12 on the third most attempts (179). Only eight teams in the country are better. Its 299.8 yards per game are the second most passing yards in the conference and 19 th in FBS. As for West Virginia, it’s ranked 15 th in the league and 121 st in the country in completion percentage. It is last in the conference in pass attempts at just 88. Its 178 ypg are also last in the Big 12. That ranks 117 th in FBS. The Mountaineers don’t defend the pass very well, either. They’re allowing 288.2 ypg, suggesting that Arizona could easily meet its average this week. That’s also last in the Big 12. Meanwhile, Arizona is giving up 75 ypg less at 213.2. WVU makes up for that by having the 3 rd ranked rushing offense in the country with 294 ypg on the ground, almost twice as many as Arizona’s 151.6 ypg. That’s a problem the Wildcats conquered just last week when Cincinnati came to town. The Bearcats came to Tucson averaging 270 ypg on the ground. Arizona held them to a season low of 74. None of the Bearcats’ runs went for more than 21 yards after breaking off 53-yard gains against both Miami (OH) and Kansas State the previous two weeks. The shortest “big run” they had prior to that was 31 yards in their season opener. The Wildcats also showed their defensive prowess on the ground against BYU, even if it didn’t result in the win. The Cougars average 235.5 rushing ypg, which is good for 16 th in the country. UA held them almost 90 yards under that at 248 in week two. BYU may lose some of its rushing luster over the next month with LJ Martin injured, but that doesn’t take away from Arizona’s effort against a full-strength Cougar running attack. Can Arizona reproduce that in a game that is across the country and likely has some extra emotional baggage for the WVU head coach? From a statistical standpoint, it’s definitely within the realm of possibility. While WVU doesn’t defend Arizona’s strength very well, the Wildcats do defend the Mountaineers’ strength well. UA has the third best rushing defense in the Big 12, allowing just 79 ypg. That comes in at 11 th in the country. Opponents average just 2.97 yards per rushing attempt. The negatives for Arizona are the travel, kickoff time, and the general emotion that’s likely to be on the other sideline. Stats say the Wildcats could win, but those things might make it closer than it would otherwise be. Ezra Amacher — Arizona wins 31- 28 Traveling to the Eastern Time Zone for a noon kickoff that’s really 9 a.m. for the visitors from Tucson makes this a trickier game to pick than it might appear on the surface. First, the opponent. West Virginia has been inconsistent at home under Rich Rod and its last game in Morgantown resulted in a 41-24 loss to Oklahoma State. The Mountaineers are in desperation mode after starting 0-2 in Big 12 play following last week’s crushing loss at Iowa State. Rich Rod indicated postgame that his defensive coordinator is having trouble fixing what’s broken. It’s safe to say West Virginia players and coaches are feeling the heat at the moment, and a third straight loss would a message for what direction the program is heading under Rodriguez. I think Arizona’s defensive game plan will go a long ways in determining the outcome of the game. If Danny Gonzales and his staff put forth a plan to stymie the Mountaineers rushing attack, then the Wildcats should leave with a hard-earned win. Considering how well last week went, I’m going to ride with Danny G and Co. until proven otherwise. Adam Green — Arizona wins 38 -24 Before the season started I had this game as a loss for Arizona. Much like my colleague Juan below, I felt like the Cats traveling across the country to face a RichRod offense — without even knowing the kickoff time — would be too much to handle. Then Arizona obliterated Cincinnati and West Virginia’s defense has shown to be, well, offensive. Understanding that Arizona may have some struggles without any of its starting receivers, I’m thinking the Cats should still have little trouble moving the ball and putting up points in this one. The only real question is if Danny Gonzales’ defense will be up to the task of slowing down an offense that, when it’s right, is incredibly difficult to stop. If Arizona can limit turnovers and create long fields for the Mountaineers there should be just enough opportunity to put some distance between the teams on the scoreboard, and given the early kickoff we should have a pretty good idea early on if this one is going to go the Wildcats’ way. Juan Serrano — West Virginia wins 35-27 I had this game marked down as a loss in my preseason record prediction. I was called crazy on social media for this prediction but now it is not looking so unrealistic that Arizona could lose on Saturday. This line of thinking is not due to the Wildcats not playing well or anything like that because through five games they have looked solid. It’s more so due to the fact that the Mountaineers are better than most people thought they would be. I saw West Virginia’s improvement coming and thought it could present an issue for Arizona. Fans in Tucson know just how much former head coach Rich Rodriguez loves to run the football, and this season he has his Mountaineers as the third best rushing attack in the country. Danny Gonzales ’ defense was up to the task last week against Cincinnati, but this is a whole new challenge. Michael Hawkins Jr. is a difference maker and can be dangerous both on the ground and through the air. I believe the secondary’s discipline will be tested in a major way this week, and will struggle. Noah Fifita will need to execute an efficient offensive performance to more than likely keep up with West Virginia on the scoreboard. If the run game can continue progressing as it has over the last two weeks, then Arizona could possibly control the clock. However, I believe that Rodriguez will have his guys motivated to play extremely hard after two very tough losses. The former coach of the Wildcats will get a little bit of payback on Saturday, and West Virginia will earn it’s first conference win of the year and move to 2-0 overall against Arizona. Brandon Combs — Arizona wins 38-21 I would be lying if I said that Morgantown was an easy place to play. Even so, there’s one glaring issue for West Virginia, their terrible defense. They haven’t faced an offense quite like Arizona and a QB like Noah Fifita . Last week, we saw what the Arizona offense can be when it is actually humming. And it looks great, even with three starting wide receivers out due to injury. If the offensive line has a good game, like I think they will, the running game will be able to establish some momentum and Noah will be able to pick the leaky Mountaineer secondary apart. Defensively, I think this game will be a challenge for Danny Gonzales. It would be silly to think otherwise. However, much like the offense, last week showed us what the defense can do when it’s operating on high octane. Gonzales’s crew played their most physical game and shut down a great Cincinnati rushing attack. I don’t think they’ll be able to shut down Rich Rodriguez’s run game, but I predict they will be able to disrupt it enough to degrade the offense. Michael Hawkins Jr. is a stud in the run game, but he isn’t much of an issue through the air. Arizona proved they can negatively impact a mobile quarterback last week, and I expect similar success this Saturday. Brian Pedersen — Arizona wins 38-34 Like Washington State, this is another game that I picked Arizona to lose prior to the season. But that was before I saw just how bad West Virginia’s defense is, and it’s bad. If the Wildcats don’t score more than 30 points in this game it’s because of their own mistakes, not for lack of opportunities. As good as the UA defense has been, and it’s been really good particularly against the run, to expect to shut down RichRod’s rushing attack is foolish. The man knows how to scheme a ground game, and if quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. can also complete some passes this will be a shootout. It will all come down to Noah Fifita and how he gels with the retooled receiving corps. Mandatory Credit: Danny Wild-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Doug Joubert Thu, October 8, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Tulane 2026 Football Schedule 6:30PM, 10/16 In a battle of colors Saturday morning in West Point, the Tulane Green Wave open the defense of their American Conference 2025 championship by visiting the Army Black Knights. Both teams enter the contest at 2-2 on the season. Team Schedules The Wave has lost its road contests against ACC defending champion Duke to open the season, then versus Big-12 opponent Kansas State two weeks later. Sandwiched between and after the two trips were home contests against Sun Belt teams, which Tulane claimed victories in both: South Alabama in the home opener and Southern Miss two weeks ago. The Green Wave had an open date last Saturday before its conference opener this weekend. Army opened the season at home with a 56-point shellacking of Bryant University out of the Coastal Athletic. The Black Knights followed with an American Conference loss at Michie Stadium versus South Florida, an early open date, then a league victory at Temple before falling at Louisiana Tech last weekend. See the PFF comparisons between Army and Tulane here. The Black Knights opened a 3.5-point favorite over the Green Wave earlier this week. That number has dropped to 3-point Army advantage since Monday. As of this writing, 81% of the money bet is on Army, giving the points to Tulane. Tulane Has Something to Prove: Our On SI Tulane Prognostication This 2026 version of Green Wave football has, if anything, been consistently inconsistent. Open the season with your new starting quarterback, who is replaced after 30-minutes, whose replacement is replaced a little over two-and-half games later, and whose replacement of the replacement is replaced for one play. Show an erratic rushing offense that can slash opponents with gigantic games from various running backs, but have nothing on a regular basis . Big passing plays to big players, but with drops and throws that sometimes don't come close, showing communication and concentration issues. Offensive and defensive fronts that are growing and progressing, but is their growth rate fast enough? Stop an opponent with three-and-outs on defense on consecutive drives, then have huge rushing gaps open in the defensive front seven or wide open receivers in the secondary. To have this much variety in results is confusing and awkward. There is plenty of talent on this team. With 60-returnees from the 2025 playoff team and some solid additions, think Jaylin Lucas, Fat Hill, Macho Stephenson, Ed Smith IV , this team should be hitting stride. But it's not. Instead, it is showing how consistently inconsistent it can be, which you cannot do against a team like Army. The Black Knights are the least penalized team in the American Conference only getting 16-flags on the season. They are the 5th least in all the NCAA. They do not make mistakes. If you are inconsistent, the discipline of Army will expose that, and expose it quickly. No matter how much coaches and players talk about defending the Black Knights option, it's another thing to actually do it. To defend it will take that word we keep on bringing up: consistency. We have not seen that from this Tulane team this year. They have to prove that they can be a team that does things well and does them on a regular basis. They have yet to do so. We think the big play will be open for Tulane, as the Black Knights give up more yards per play than any other team in the American, almost 7-yards a pop. If the Wave offensive front is able to open the holes for the running back and protect the quarterback, whoever that may be (we believe it should be Trace Johnson , but we've been wrong before), there will be big chunks available. However, we also believe Army's multiple option attack will be the undoing of the Green Wave defense. On SI Tulane Pick: Army 35 - Tulane 28 Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Tulane Green Wave at Army Black Knights Prediction, Picks & Odds for Week 6
2026 Week 6 Preview: Tulane Green Wave @ Army Black Knights
picks.blurb: 2026 Week 6 Preview: Tulane Green Wave @ Army Black Knights | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty October 13, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications American Conference Two high-powered rushing attacks meet in West Point for the first time since the 2024 American title game. Time and date: Saturday, October 10 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: CBS Sports Network Location: Michie Stadium — West Point, NY Spread: Army (-3.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Tulane leads, 14-10-1 Last meeting: Tulane 24, Army 17 — October 18, 2025 Current streak: Tulane, 1 (2025) Setting the scene Even before sharing the American Conference, Army and Tulane were famliar opponents, squaring off 19 times from 1996 through 2020. The Black Knights then joined the American in 2024 and instantly ran the league, rattling off an 8-0 conference record before handling Tulane in the conference championship game. That was the only time in the last four years Tulane didn’t serve as the conference title host. With first-year head coach Will Hall in the fold, the Green Wave hope to host the American Championship for a fourth time in five years. To achieve that goal, it starts with defeating Army at Michie Stadium in this conference opener. Tulane Green Wave outlook Tulane (2-2, 0-0 American) split its non-conference slate, falling to Duke and Kansas State by double-digits on the road, while escaping Sun Belt opponents South Alabama and Southern Miss at home with late fourth quarter heroics. The biggest question entering this game, asks: who starts at quarterback? Zeon Chriss-Gremillion was Tulane’s Week 1 starter, but the Green Wave moved to Kadin Semonza for Weeks 2 through 4. But at the end of the last outing against Southern Miss, head coach Will Hall changed quarterbacks from Semonza to true freshman Trace Johnson in the fourth quarter. Johnson provided a spark in the come-from-behind victory, but his sample size remains small, completing just 2-of-5 passes for 35 yards without a single rushing attempt. The passing game unquestionably needs a boost. Tulane ranks 105th in the FBS in passing offense, completing just 54.2 percent of attempts with three touchdowns against one interception. The pass protection has been lacking too, allowing the 11th-most sacks per game in the country at 3.3. However, the Green Wave can dominate on the ground, and they do it with several different weapons. Running backs Jaylin Lucas and Maurice Turner each rushed for 200+ yards in the first four weeks, and the group gets even deeper as Jamauri McClure — Tulane’s starting running back during its 2025 College Football Playoff run — is slated to make his season debut. Tulane’s strength last season was its run defense, but the Green Wave have fallen off in that department, entering this matchup against the No. 1 rushing offense ranked 125th — allowing 191 yards per game on the ground. Losing star outside linebacker Chris Rodgers certainly doesn’t help, but the Green Wave still present veteran linebackers Makai Williams and Dickson Agu, who will be essential to countering this option. Army Black Knights outlook Army (2-2, 1-1 American) is already preparing for its third conference game. The Black Knights’ first two conference matchups were decided by the thinnest margins, featuring a lead change in the final two minutes. Army wound up on the wrong side of that late lead change in Week 2 when South Florida converted a late fourth down for a game-winning touchdown. But two weeks later, the Black Knights returned the favor at Temple. One-score games are customary for Army. Nine of the Black Knights’ last 10 matchups against FBS competition were decided by one score, and eight of the last nine were decided by four points or fewer — including every FBS matchup this season. Army’s option offense is in a familiar spot at first in the country in rushing yards per game at 334, while averaging the sixth-most yards per carry (6.4) in the FBS. Cale Hellums, who led all quarterbacks in rushing last year, remains the unit’s leading rusher with 301 yards, and his rushing performance dictates the result more than anyone else. In Army’s two wins, he has 191 yards and five touchdowns on a 6.6 average. In the losses to South Florida and Louisiana Tech, he combined for 110 yards and one touchdown on a 3.0 average. The Black Knights’ other ball carriers in the option attack include running back Godspower Nwawuihe and the explosive slot backs Samari Howard (293 rushing yards on a 10.9 average) and Zach Mundell (159 yards on a 14.5 average). However, Nwawuihe’s status remains unknown after he missed the Louisiana Tech game, which could make Carson Smith and Jake Rendina the downhill threats. Army’s defense allowed over 500 yards to Louisiana Tech, and that remains the team’s greatest struggle. away.headline: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense
away.blurb: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense As they practiced on Tuesday for game prep coming off their bye week, Green Wave running back Jamauri McClure was a sight for sore eyes out there, participating in team drills without a non-contact jersey for the first time since he went down with a fractured foot in fall camp. This year's room looks a lot different in comparison. Maurice Turner is playing his best football right now. Jaylin Lucas has gotten some work out in space a bit more this week of prep. Johnnie Daniels has shown that he can throw a killer block as much as he can shoot through a gap. However, the return of McClure is what fans have been clamoring for since the news first got out that he was hurt. Now that he's had ample time to recover, his return should be a major boost for a Tulane offense looking to make the most out of and stretch out what should be expected to be limited possessions against the Army Black Knights Saturday. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Maddy Hudak Tue, October 6, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The best ability is often availability, and the Tulane Green Wave certainly have some good news on that front ahead of American conference play. But while head coach Will Hall told media members on Tuesday that he and the team feel that they're a better football team than when we last talked to and saw them last two weeks back, they have a lot to prove on the road to kick off their conference slate. An essential thing they're looking for is an identity on offense. Well, a lot of that can be solved by a strong rush attack that McClure instantaneously boosts. When McClure started taking over the starting running back job towards the end of the year last season, it was clear that he had a different gear and set of traits than what we were seeing from that room. Further good news on that front is that nothing appears to be up with Turner, who ended up limping a bit at the end of his 74-yard touchdown run against the Southern Miss Golden Eagles, as he also was practicing in full with no non-contact jersey. But the true finesse of that room lies with McClure. Another major returnee was wide receiver Zycarl Lewis, who got injured during the season opener against the Duke Blue Devils and hasn't practiced or played since. He was also not in a non-contact jersey on the practice field Tuesday. McClure averaged an impressive 6.5 yards per carry last season. The redshirt sophomore had eight total carries until Week 12 of last year against the FAU Owls. In the final five games of the season, he added 75 touches for 83 total carries for 540 yards and two touchdowns.

away.blurb: "We're at a point where we're going into conference play and we know we've got to play better," Hall told us at his weekly media conference. "We've not played our best yet. That's a negative, but also a positive that our best is still out there. You should get better as the season goes on....We feel like we're a much better football team right now than we were last time we talked to you (two weeks ago)," Expect the highly anticipated return of last year's breakout running back Jamauri McClure . The then-freshman sensation rushed for 540-yards, though really being used from about the midway point in the year on. He averaged 6.5-yards every time he touched the ball in 2025. McClure was injured during Fall practice getting surgery on his left foot to repair damage done. He's been sidelined all this year, with the Wave targeting the American opener as his season debut. Receiver Zycarl Lewis , who was hurt during the Duke game, is set to return as well, recovering from a leg injury. Though Hall listed both tight end Ty Thompson and linebacker Chris Rodgers as doubtful for Saturday, fans should not plan on either of them contributing this weekend. Thompson is nursing a leg injury that has forced him to miss extended time, and Rodgers has a foot injury that is putting the star backer on the sidelines for the foreseeable future. Tulane Prepares for Army Option, Welcomes Back 2025 Star RB from Injury Skip to main content On SI The Tulane football team opens the defense of its American Conference 2025 championship on Saturday with a trip to West Point to visit the United States Military Academy. Kickoff from Michie Stadium is set for 11:00 a.m. CT and can be seen on the CBS Sports Network. After a bye week to rest up and prepare, Green Wave head coach Will Hall is feeling good about his squad's preparedness. "The advantages of when our bye week fell is it is right smack dab in the middle of our season," Hall shared Tuesday. "We had five weeks of fall camp, then four games. That's nine weeks. Now we've got a bye week and eight games left. So, it's right in the middle. It is right before conference play and it's right before we play an option team. I think those are advantages The league opener is like a new season for Hall and his team, as they get ready for what is essentially a restart to their season. "We know how important it is to get off on the right foot and be 1-0 in conference play," Hall said Tuesday, "so our young men are taking that very seriously. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Brent Venables and the sputtering Sooners face a massive test against Colin Simmons and a dominant Longhorns defense in Dallas Getty Images No. 1 Texas hopes to win the Red River Rivalry matchup against Oklahoma for the third straight time Saturday afternoon at the State Fair of Texas in Dallas. The Longhorns reached No. 1 for the third straight season under Steve Sarkisian, this time after outlasting Ohio State in Week 2. The Longhorns rank among the best defenses in college football , and field quarterback Arch Manning . The Sooners also rank among the best defenses in the sport, but the offense has backslid dramatically under coach Brent Venables. Oklahoma is off to a 2-2 start after a 41-13 loss to No. 2 Georgia last week as the program turned the ball over four times, including a miserable fumble by quarterback John Mateer that was returned for a touchdown. Oklahoma has lost three of four Red River Rivalries under Brent Venables, averaging only 3.0 points per game in those losses. Texas won 23-6 last year as the Sooners turned the ball over three times and were held without a touchdown. Where to watch Texas vs. Oklahoma live Date : Saturday, Oct. 10 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Cotton Bowl -- Dallas TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Texas vs. Oklahoma: Need to know Historically bad offense: Oklahoma's offense has been a disaster through the first several weeks, averaging an astonishing 11.5 points per game against Power Four competition. While quarterback John Mateer has been the primary target, the Sooners are averaging only 2.9 yards per carry, the worst mark in the SEC. Oklahoma failed to score a point against Georgia until trailing 28-0 in the third quarter, and Texas's defense rates higher in many metrics. Rise of Simmons: Texas defensive end Colin Simmons has been regarded as one of the best in the sport, but his performance against Tennessee will go down in the record books. The junior set a Texas record with 5.5 sacks against freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon , which ultimately led to Brandon's benching one week later. Simmons had 29.5 tackles for loss and 21 sacks in his first two seasons, and hopes to build on that as a junior. Which Arch do we get?: Texas quarterback Arch Manning is a lightning rod because of his famous last name, but the junior oscillates between brilliance and inconsistency -- even in the same game. In the first half against Ohio State, Manning connected on only 7 of 14 passes for 44 yards. Against Texas A&M last season, he was 5-of-15 for 28 yards. Oklahoma is probably not good enough to take advantage, but Manning needs to start faster for Texas to maintain its No. 1 ranking. Texas vs. Oklahoma prediction, picks It's always dangerous to bet on a big line in a major rivalry game, but it's getting harder than ever to trust Brent Venables' squad to come through. Three of Oklahoma's four games against Texas under Venables cleared a 17-point margin of victory, and this Sooners squad might be the worst one yet. College football sometimes surprises you, but... this would be a surprise. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Texas vs. Oklahoma Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB One of college football's best rivalries will take center stage in Dallas, Texas, on Saturday afternoon. The No. 1 Texas Longhorns will battle the Oklahoma Sooners in the 122nd edition of the Red River Rivalry. Texas won the last two meetings, and this year's matchup mirrors last year's. The defenses should control the game's outcome, as they both rank in the SEC's top five in points allowed. Anything can happen in a rivalry game, so here are three bold predictions for Texas vs. Oklahoma. Cam Coleman Eclipses 100 Receiving Yards Texas Longhorns wide receiver Cam Coleman. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cam Coleman has four receiving touchdowns this season, but the yardage hasn't been there. The junior wideout has 208 receiving yards. Coleman's season-high (70) came in the season opener against Texas State. Cam Coleman has four receiving touchdowns this season, but the yardage hasn't been there. The junior wideout has 208 receiving yards. Coleman's season-high (70) came in the season opener against Texas State. On Saturday, I think he eclipses that total and becomes the first Texas receiver to reach 100 yards in a game this season. However, the Longhorns' offense has been sluggish, and the Sooners will not make life easy. Texas will need a couple of big plays from its offense, and Coleman is the perfect player to do so. I predict Oklahoma will try to stop the run in the second half, and Coleman will be fully unleashed. The Defense Scores Their First Touchdown of the Season Texas Longhorns edge Colin Simmons reacts after recovering a fumble. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Longhorns' defense has forced six turnovers this season. Will Muschamp's group was outstanding against Tennessee, sacking Faizon Brandon 10 times, but Texas hasn't scored a defensive touchdown. The Longhorns' defense has forced six turnovers this season. Will Muschamp's group was outstanding against Tennessee, sacking Faizon Brandon 10 times, but Texas hasn't scored a defensive touchdown. The Sooners' offense is struggling mightily. It's hard to imagine John Mateer easily moving the ball against Texas. I think the Longhorns will pressure Mateer into a mistake, and Texas will capitalize with a touchdown. Points could be hard to come by on Saturday, so if the defense can score points, that would be a massive advantage for the Longhorns. Hollywood Smothers Outgains Oklahoma's Rushing Total by Himself Texas Longhorns running back Hollywood Smothers. picks.blurb: Kirk Herbstreit Hesitatingly Picks Winner for Texas-Oklahoma Week 6 College Football Game Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Given that Texas is the No. 1 team in the nation and Oklahoma has been one of the SEC's biggest disappointments, this season's verion of the Red River Rivalry isn't necessarily being considered one of the best games in college football this week. But don't tell that conclusion to ESPN's Kirk Herbstreit, who thinks the ingredients are in place for a battle in this season's matchup. Herbstreit's Red River Pick While Texas is a solid road favorite against 2-2 Oklahoma, Herbstreit was thoughtful and reluctant to enter his decision on this game... before ultimately picking the Longhorns. Herbstreit certainly doesn't think the action goes down without a fight. "I think OU's going to make this game competitive," said Herbstreit on ESPN's College GameDay . "Because it's a rivalry game and you expect one team to win, that's always a dangerous receipe to me." Texas's Struggles QB Arch Manning could struggle, per Kirk Herbstreit, if Oklahoma can put him in long-yardage situations. (Randy Sartin-Imagn Images) | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Texas is the obvious favorite, but with two wins over ranked teams by a combined four points, the Longhorns haven't been a juggernaut, particularly on offense. QB Arch Manning has been underwhelming, currently sitting 10th of 16 qualifying SEC quarterbacks in QB rating. Manning's 7.5 yards per pass attempt ranks 11th of the passers. Manning is 14th in the league in passing yardage and his 7 touchdown passes ties for 11th. That said, Texas's offensive concerns still are minor compared to the issues at Oklahoma. QB Arch Manning has been underwhelming, currently sitting 10th of 16 qualifying SEC quarterbacks in QB rating. Manning's 7.5 yards per pass attempt ranks 11th of the passers. Manning is 14th in the league in passing yardage and his 7 touchdown passes ties for 11th. That said, Texas's offensive concerns still are minor compared to the issues at Oklahoma. Herbstreit Loves Oklahoma Defense Oklahoma is next to last in the SEC in scoring offense (22 points per game) and is dead last in total offense (321.3 yards per game). That's 57 yards per game behind 12th place Texas, and QB John Mateer has looked particularly lost with four interceptions on the young season and a performance so ugly against New Mexico that he admitted that he had to hear the crowd to clue him in on an open receiver on one play. While Oklahoma's offense has been woeful, Herbstreit notes, "Their defense has been playing at a championship level." Considering the occasional lapses in concentration from the Texas offense, Hebrstreit saw that as an advantage. "If they can get Arch [Manning] to 3rd and five, 3rd and seven, they can create havoc on him. They're one of the best third-down defenses in the country." Indeed, Oklahoma leads the SEC and currently ranks third nationally in allowing opponents to connect on just 23.1% of third downs (12 for 52). The Sooners are second in the conference in total defense, surrendering just 238 yards per game. The Final Pick Herbstreit seemed to give genuine thought to picking the Sooners for the upset. "I think this is a close game," he said. "I think OU's defense can keep them within striking distance. I just don't think they can win, with the offense the way they are playing." picks.blurb: Paul Finebaum Predicts Texas-Oklahoma Winner in Eye-Catching Fashion Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Paul Finebaum is many things, but not above a little casual trolling is certainly one of them. Known as one of the preeminent voices of SEC media well before his time began with ESPN, the network leans heavily on Finebaum's SEC expertise. And with the relatively recent expansion of the SEC, plenty of fan bases are getting to know Finebaum more and more. Add Oklahoma and Texas to that group, as the two former Big 12 stalwarts are getting to see more and more of Finebaum. This week on SEC Nation , Finebaum weighed in on the 2026 edition of the Red River Rivalry in his typical fashion. The four SEC Nation cast members weighed in on the Oklahoma/Texas game. Despite the show being in Norman, Oklahoma this week, the first three cast members went with the conventional wisdom and picked the Texas Longhorns who are favored by around a touchdown in the rivalry battle with the Sooners. Finebaum made it more interesting. Finebaum's Take "I keep hearing that you have a rivalry game and anything can happen. And you Sooners know that, right?" asked Finebaum. Having stoked the crowd, he then turned heel and disappointed them. "But I don't think you really have to factor that in because there's one team over here going up," continued Finebaum. "There's another team going down. And the Sooners are going down. Hook 'em, Horns!" THE PICKS ARE IN‼️ The SEC Nation crew make their picks for the Red River Rivalry 🤠 pic.twitter.com/8PCoNgnNNh Oklahoma's Troubles Finebaum delivered the unanimous vote for Texas and it's unsurprising as the top-ranked Longhorns travel to a 2-2 Oklahoma team that has had massive problems on offense this season. Since a 51-0 win over UTEP in Week 1, Oklahoma has scored just 10, 14, and 13 points in the past three games, which included a loss to Michigan and a 41-13 loss to Georgia. The Sooners failed to gain 300 yards in any of those three games. An 8-0 ESPN pick for Texas While Texas's offense has been somewhat inconsistent, the Longhorn defense has had enough strength to hold off Ohio State and Tennessee-- albeit by a combined four-point margin. While Oklahoma has an even more stout defense, the conventional wisdom is that a balanced Texas team can probably score enough points to win. While pregame pickers on both SEC Nation and College GameDay took time to shout out the OU defense , a unanimous 8-0 verdict between the two shows had the Longhorns winning. That said, few seemed to have as much fun in stoking the crowd as did Finebaum. Loading recommendations... Texas has beaten Oklahoma in three of Brent Venables' four Red River Rivalry games by an average of 32.3 points. In those three wins, the Longhorns held the Sooners to fewer than seven points, thanks to dominant defensive performances. This year's Texas defense might be the best one yet, ranking No. 3 in net adjusted EPA per play , No. 11 in success rate (36.5%), and No. 16 in havoc rate (20.6%). Oklahoma put up just 258 yards on Texas last year, and the Longhorns' defense is better this time around. It's ranked No. 5 by SP+ and has allowed more than 17 points once. That was to Ohio State and Heisman Trophy odds favorite Jeremiah Smith, and it allowed just three points in the second half to the Buckeyes. away.headline: Oklahoma Sooners' injury report for matchup vs. Texas Longhorns opened eyes to an issue that's been going on since 2024
away.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners head into the Red River Rivalry against the Texas Longhorns with a long injury list. At this point, what's new? Banged-up rosters have become the norm for OU over the last few years. Ever since the SEC's player availability reports started in 2024, the Sooners have almost always carried a health disadvantage into game day. George Stoia of SoonersScoop.com pointed out a number that puts it in perspective, and I think it's worth mentioning. Stoia laid it out: OU averages 10.25 players on the initial availability report since it began in 2024. Its opponents averaged 6.68. OU has had fewer players on the initial report only once-the College Football Playoff game against Alabama. The Sooners had 6 players on that report. That feels about right. Nobody needs to stat-check it, either. Thursday's availability report for OU vs. Texas tells the same story . The Sooners have five players listed as out, two doubtful, one questionable, and five probable. Oklahoma – Out: Taylor Heim, Trell Harris, Xavier Robinson, Jacobe Johnson, Fred Hinton – Doubtful: Trynae Washington, Michael Fasusi – Questionable: Eddie Pierre-Louis – Probable: Jer'Michael Carter, Cole Sullivan, Michael Boganowski, Owen Heinecke, Jack Van Dorselaer. Texas – Out: Kaliq Lockett, Jordan Coleman, Zion Williams – Questionable: Justus Terry That's 13 names for Oklahoma and four for Texas. That's just how it is for the Sooners every week. When the Wednesday report came out, some fans were legitimately concerned. The list looked worse than it did heading into the Georgia game, even though OU had a bye week in between. More names showed up after a week off, not fewer. So fans scrambled to figure out how a team gets more injured during a bye. Fair enough, that's a decent question to ask. How does that work? I have no idea. Most likely, some players got more banged up in the Georgia game, and we just didn't know about it going into the bye. That's why building depth in the NIL era matters so much. You're going to have injuries, and OU seems to have more than anybody. Maybe that perception is right, maybe it's wrong. Regardless, the depth has to be better. You can sit here and look at this issue all you want and try to figure out what's going wrong internally. The game still has to be played. Texas isn't going to skip the Red River Rivalry because Oklahoma has a lot of guys on the report. You'd love to see the Sooners keep building their depth so the next man up can carry more of the load. For now, the Longhorns definitely have the advantage. Texas is already the No. 1-ranked team in the country, and the Sooners are coming in with really bad football. With 13 players on the availability report, OU will need its backups to step up. home.headline: Oklahoma Sooners' injury report for matchup vs. Texas Longhorns opened eyes to an issue that's been going on since 2024
home.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners head into the Red River Rivalry against the Texas Longhorns with a long injury list. At this point, what's new? Banged-up rosters have become the norm for OU over the last few years. Ever since the SEC's player availability reports started in 2024, the Sooners have almost always carried a health disadvantage into game day. George Stoia of SoonersScoop.com pointed out a number that puts it in perspective, and I think it's worth mentioning. Stoia laid it out: OU averages 10.25 players on the initial availability report since it began in 2024. Its opponents averaged 6.68. OU has had fewer players on the initial report only once-the College Football Playoff game against Alabama. The Sooners had 6 players on that report. That feels about right. Nobody needs to stat-check it, either. Thursday's availability report for OU vs. Texas tells the same story . The Sooners have five players listed as out, two doubtful, one questionable, and five probable. Oklahoma – Out: Taylor Heim, Trell Harris, Xavier Robinson, Jacobe Johnson, Fred Hinton – Doubtful: Trynae Washington, Michael Fasusi – Questionable: Eddie Pierre-Louis – Probable: Jer'Michael Carter, Cole Sullivan, Michael Boganowski, Owen Heinecke, Jack Van Dorselaer. Texas – Out: Kaliq Lockett, Jordan Coleman, Zion Williams – Questionable: Justus Terry That's 13 names for Oklahoma and four for Texas. That's just how it is for the Sooners every week. When the Wednesday report came out, some fans were legitimately concerned. The list looked worse than it did heading into the Georgia game, even though OU had a bye week in between. More names showed up after a week off, not fewer. So fans scrambled to figure out how a team gets more injured during a bye. Fair enough, that's a decent question to ask. How does that work? I have no idea. Most likely, some players got more banged up in the Georgia game, and we just didn't know about it going into the bye. That's why building depth in the NIL era matters so much. You're going to have injuries, and OU seems to have more than anybody. Maybe that perception is right, maybe it's wrong. Regardless, the depth has to be better. You can sit here and look at this issue all you want and try to figure out what's going wrong internally. The game still has to be played. Texas isn't going to skip the Red River Rivalry because Oklahoma has a lot of guys on the report. You'd love to see the Sooners keep building their depth so the next man up can carry more of the load. For now, the Longhorns definitely have the advantage. Texas is already the No. 1-ranked team in the country, and the Sooners are coming in with really bad football. With 13 players on the availability report, OU will need its backups to step up. In 2022, the Bruins started the season 6-0 before going to Oregon, but that UCLA team was a bit of a mirage. No, this isn't at the 1998 level yet, when the team was 10-0 and deep in the national title hunt before losing in a historic 49-45 thriller against Edgerrin James and Miami. And no, this UCLA team isn't there yet in Bob Chesney's first season, but if it pulls this off, everything changes. Oregon got back to being Oregon again with a 41-27 win over USC, but Dante Moore is out, Dylan Raiola is in, and this is when it has to flex at home and show just how much the Week 2 loss to Oklahoma State was a blip. UCLA vs Oregon: Quick Hits Oregon gets three home games in the next four weeks. It plays unbeaten UCLA this week, hosts currently unbeaten Nebraska next week, goes to Illinois, and then hosts Northwestern before traveling to Ohio State. UCLA plays three home games in a row after this, hosting Wisconsin, Michigan State, and Nevada before going to Minnesota. Oregon has won five straight in the series since 2017, last winning 34-13 in 2024. The one time it had a problem with a ground attack was against Oklahoma State, when it got hammered for 237 yards and close to six yards per carry. UCLA is fourth in the nation in rushing, averaging 281.5 yards per game and seven yards per carry. Oregon's run defense has had time to prepare – the loss to the Cowboys really was an aberration – but the Bruins get physical and grind teams down. Purdue's Ryan Browne went off for 378 yards and three scores in UCLA's 52-38 win. Dylan Raiola is about to have a day. UCLA has a pass rush and should be able to get to Raiola a bit against an Oregon offensive line that hasn't been a rock so far, but the passing game will blow up. UCLA vs Oregon Prediction, Betting Lines The key to UCLA is the ability to hang around and then take over in the second half. The problem is that it won't be able to do that so easily against an Oregon defense that's No. 1 in the nation in third down stops. The Bruins are going to be a problem for the Big Ten the rest of the season – seriously, even with a loss here, they still have a great shot to be in the CFP mix – but Oregon really is one of the ten best teams in college football, and when it has to midway through the second half, it'll show why. Here's what to look for ahead of the ranked matchup. Oregon vs. UCLA scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks are the only team in the country to average over 300 passing yards per game without an interception, split between starter Dante Moore and backup Dylan Raiola. Oregon ranks third nationally in passing yards per game and has done a good job of avoiding turnovers. If the Ducks can dictate tempo through the air, create explosive plays and avoid turnovers, they should win this game. Why UCLA has an advantage: The Bruins, to this point in the season, have run the ball much more consistently than the Ducks. UCLA ranks in the top five nationally in rush yards per play, rushing touchdowns and rushing yards per game. Led by standout back Wayne Knight, the Bruins average nearly 7 yards per carry. The Ducks rank toward the back half in the country around 4.6 yards per rushing attempt. If the Bruins can establish their ground game and control the tempo of this game, they'll have a chance to spring an upset. After suffering a concussion against USC, Moore returned to practice this week, but his status moving forward is unclear. Oregon's first mandatory injury report will be released Wednesday night and should offer clarity on his availability moving forward. Elsewhere, receiver Jeremiah McClellan is expected to be out still while Jalen Lott could make his return after a hand surgery sidelined him through Oregon's first four games. For UCLA: The Bruins' injury report will also be released Wednesday night, but several banged-up players made their returns in UCLA's last outing against Maryland in Week 4. Receiver Aidan Mizell, DB Jhase McMillan and tight end Josh Phifer were all listed as questionable or probable and shifted to available on game day. The Bruins are one of the top rushing teams in the country. Though Oregon's offense has been able to move the ball effectively through the air, it will absolutely need to run the ball better than it has to beat the Bruins. away.headline: Report: UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava expected to miss remainder of season with knee injury
away.blurb: ESPN’s Pete Thamel later reported that Iamaleava is out indefinitely with the injury, but added that no timetable has been set yet. Any final timeline is pending an upcoming medical evaluation. What is known, though, is that Iamaleava will not be suiting up for the Bruins anytime soon. “At the end of the day, football’s football for me,” Dieffenbach said postgame. “So, I mean, the crowd can only do so much. But, we blocked it out. I’ve just been waiting for this moment. I was ready.” UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava is expected to miss the remainder of the season due to the knee injury he suffered against Oregon on Saturday, CBS Sports first reported . Iamaleava was instrumental in UCLA ‘s stellar 5-0 (3-0) start to the season, which has propelled them to No. 12 in this week’s AP Poll (highest ranking since Nov. 2022). $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Through five games this season, Iamaleava had completed 62.1% of his passes for 982 yards and four touchdowns with four interceptions. On the ground, he rushed for 144 yards and another score. UCLA will now turn to backup Ty Dieffenbach , who took over for the Bruins following Iamaleava’s injury on Saturday. In relief, Dieffenbach completed 3/6 passes for 43 yards and one touchdown against Oregon . That touchdown pass was the difference in UCLA ‘s 17-15 win over the then-No. 13 ranked Ducks, which marked the Bruins’ first since 2017. “When someone goes down and someone has to step up, I say it every single time… you’re either exposed or you’re revealed,” UCLA head coach Bob Chesney said postgame . “One of the two is going to happen when your number gets called. For Ty to step up in that moment when Nico couldn’t go, he put himself in a spot where he was revealed for knowing the run game and getting us into the touchdown pass.” Ty Dieffenbach expected to be propelled to UCLA’s starter Ty Dieffenbach transferred to UCLA this offseason after spending the 2025 season at Cal Poly . There, Dieffenbach completed 92/162 passes for 1,305 yards and nine touchdowns (with nine interceptions). Prior to his stint at Cal Poly , Dieffenbach spent the first two seasons of his collegiate career at Pitt . As a member of that program, however, he did not appear in a game. The official Big Ten Preseason Media Poll projected UCLA to finish 13th in the conference in year one under former JMU head coach Bob Chesney . Five games into the season, however, the Bruins are certainly in the running to clinch a College Football Playoff berth for the first time in program history.

away.headline: Oregon HC Dan Lanning will not punish Ber Alexander for injuring UCLA’s Nico Iamaleava
away.blurb: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning has confirmed that defensive lineman Bear Alexander will not face team discipline for an apparent punch to UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava during the Ducks’ 17-15 loss on Saturday. Speaking to reporters Monday night, Lanning explained that Alexander was attempting to knock the football loose rather than deliberately strike the Bruins quarterback. The incident occurred in the second quarter at Autzen Stadium, when Iamaleava scrambled before being brought down by Alexander and Oregon linebacker Jerry Mixon. Television replays appeared to show Alexander swinging his right arm and striking Iamaleava’s helmet as the quarterback lay on the ground. The play also involved contact with the quarterback’s leg, and he subsequently suffered a knee injury that is expected to end his season. Iamaleava sustained a torn ACL, according to On3’s Pete Nakos. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the apparent punch went unpenalized during the game, footage of the incident drew widespread attention on social media afterward. Alexander finished with six tackles in the loss. UCLA head coach Bob Chesney addressed the incident during his Monday press conference, criticizing Alexander’s apparent punch. The Bruins coach did not witness the contact as it happened but reviewed the footage afterward and described the action as “egregious.” He also said there was serious concern about Iamaleava’s condition while the team awaited further information about the injury and its recovery timeline. Iamaleava momentarily returned to the field before halftime but did not play in the second half. His injury came as UCLA pursued a win that improved its record to 5-0 and was its first win at Autzen Stadium since 2004. The Bruins led 10-6 when the incident occurred and extended their advantage to 17-6 in the fourth quarter. The Ducks responded with nine points but failed to complete a game-tying two-point conversion, allowing UCLA to secure victory. Alexander’s situation also drew comparisons with the controversy surrounding Bruins linebacker Desman Stephens II, who was suspended after landing a hard hit to Oregon quarterback Dante Moore. The Big Ten has not yet announced a disciplinary decision regarding the incident. The Ducks, now 3-2 overall and 1-1 in conference play, is scheduled to host Nebraska on Saturday night at Autzen Stadium. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. home.headline: Nico Iamaleava took a punch from an Oregon defender in Week 6
home.blurb: Iamaleava suffered the injury late in the first half of UCLA's 17-15 win over Oregon . Iamaleava would briefly return before halftime but UCLA turned to Ty Dieffenbach in the second half, with the Bruins realizing that Iamaleava's injury was far more serious than initially thought. Nico Iamaleava took a punch from an Oregon defender in Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Nico Iamaleava took a punch from an Oregon defender in Week 6 Dylan McNeill, UCLA Wire Tue, October 13, 2026 at 2:07 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The season certainly took a twist on Monday for the UCLA Bruins , as it was reported that UCLA 's starting quarterback, Nico Iamaleava, will miss the remainder of the 2026 season with a leg injury . Where does this leave UCLA? The Bruins looked poised to make a College Football Playoff run but with such a giant question mark at quarterback, things are a lot less clear. UCLA could give Dieffenbach the reins or even mix in Madden Iamaleava but either quarterback is an unproven commodity in the Big Ten. To make matters worse, on the play where Iamaleava was injured, it appeared that an Oregon defender swung on Iamaleava after the UCLA quarterback was already tackled to the ground. The defender was likely trying to force a fumble but his plans failed horribly, slugging Iamaleava in the helmet. Both Dan Lanning and Bob Chesney spoke about the alleged punch by the Ducks ' Bear Alexander. "I was talking to Nico, he's like, 'They keep punching me in the face.' ... I didn't see it," Chesney said . "But when you see it, it's certainly egregious. It shouldn't be a play that's allowed to occur in this sport and it's a shame that it was missed." Unsurprisingly, Lanning viewed the play differently. "You never want to see a player get injured. I think Bear was trying to take a ball shot," Lanning said . "Obviously it's late, right? It's not the way it needs to be done. It wasn't executed the right way. Bear knows that and I think he feels bad about that." While it was a bad look for the Oregon defender to connect a punch on Iamaleava, that punch did not cause Iamaleava's season-ending injury, it was just an unfortunate situation for Iamaleava to get slugged in the face while suffering a serious leg injury.
