The last time that LSU played in Lexington, it didn't go very well for the Tigers. LSU lost 41-21 on the road to Kentucky in 2021. It was the second straight SEC loss for the Tigers under then head coach Ed Orgeron. It was a loss that all but sealed the fate of Orgeron (especially after he admitted that LSU's defensive line got out-physicaled). The Tigers will return to Lexington this weekend for a matchup against the Wildcats. And while no players remain on the roster from the 2021 LSU team, I'm sure head coach Lane Kiffin will use the loss to Kentucky in 2021 as motivation. ESPN's Cole Cubelic shares how he thinks the LSU vs Kentucky game will play out ESPN's Cole Cubelic shared some thoughts this week on the LSU vs Kentucky matchup. Cubelic noted that he likes the momentum that Kentucky has right now, but he doesn't think the Wildcats can consistently pressure Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt. "I like this game being at Kroger Field," said Cubelic . "I like the momentum Kentucky has right now. The problem is that Kentucky can't get to the quarterback, and I think Sam Leavitt has gotten better in the pocket — he was forced to (get better in the pocket) with the hamstring two weeks ago against Texas A&M. And he did it again last week. "[Leavitt] being able to find success from the pocket and Kentucky not being able to get home, that's going to be a problem. And LSU is going to score. So I think LSU gets the win. I'm not going to touch the 8.5 (points) there that LSU is favored by, but I may like the over 51.5 in this game." Joshua Nunn Sat, October 10, 2026 at 10:08 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The North Dakota State Bison take on the UNLV Rebels in Las Vegas, NV. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. ET on The CW. North Dakota State is favored by -3.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -160. The total is set at 48.5 points. Here's my North Dakota State vs. UNLV prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 10. North Dakota State vs. UNLV Pick: North Dakota State Team Total Under 25.5 My UNLV vs. North Dakota State best bet is on the Rebels' total points. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and make sure to download our Action Network app to get the latest picks and betting analysis. North Dakota State vs UNLV Odds North Dakota State vs UNLV point spread : North Dakota State -3.5 (-102), UNLV +3.5 (-120) North Dakota State vs UNLV over/under : 48.5 (-105o / -115u) North Dakota State vs UNLV moneyline : North Dakota State -160, UNLV +130 North Dakota State has been impressive this season in its first at the FBS level, and the transition has gone as well as anyone would have predicted. The Bison are 5-0 both straight up and against the spread, led by their defense, which is tied with Miami for first in the country. NDSU has allowed just 9.8 points per game this season. The Bison have remained true to the identity that brought them so much success at the FCS level, using a ball-control offense, power running game and rock-solid defense to win games. The offense isn't as explosive, dominant or dynamic as in previous seasons, but quarterback Nathan Hayes has completed 65% of his passes with 995 yards through the air and a 7:2 touchdown-to-interception ratio. The ground game has been effective and efficient without being overly explosive. NDSU is averaging 171 rushing yards per game as a team on 4.2 yards per carry. DJ Scott and Myles Mitchell garner the majority of the carries and have rushed for 512 yards between the pair with seven combined rushing scores. Jackson Williams is the most consistent receiver and has hauled in 22 passes for 358 yards this season. He'll see a decent amount of the target share in this game. The defense has been unbelievably impressive while holding four of its five opponents to 10 points or less. The Bison have been strong against the run and have held their opponents — including Air Force — to just three yards per carry and 102 yards per game on the ground. The secondary hasn't surrendered explosive plays, and only 40% of opponent red-zone trips have resulted in touchdowns. This bunch will have its hands full against UNLV on the road this week, but I expect a decent showing out of this defense. UNLV has to consider this season mildly disappointing thus far, as the Rebels dropped the season opener at home against Memphis and were embarrassed on the road at North Texas earlier in the season. Recently, however, the offense has come to life with back-to-back games, scoring 38 and 39 points in wins over Akron and Cal . The Rebels have their sights set on continuing to remain in contention for a Mountain West title. The offense is going to remain run-oriented, as Jai'Den Thomas leads the way with 383 yards and a pair of rushing scores. Thomas provides explosiveness and versatility out of the running back position and is a great complement to quarterback Jackson Arnold , who has run for 270 yards while leading the team with five rushing scores. Arnold has thrown the ball well over the last two weeks, and connecting on the downfield passes has spring-loaded the scoring for UNLV. While only 59% of his passes have been completed, Arnold creates well on the move, has thrown eight touchdown passes without an interception, and many of his incomplete passes were throwaways to avoid sacks. The eyesore has been the offensive line, which has surrendered 14 sacks and 28 tackles for loss. This group will have its work cut out for them against a strong Bison defensive front. The UNLV defense isn't a strong unit, but it has played well at times this season. Holding Hawaii to six points on the road was quite a feat, and Akron was held scoreless after halftime a couple of weeks back. Cal scored 31 points last week against this defense in completely fluky fashion. One scoring drive was a 91-yard touchdown pass where a defender fell, and another missed a tackle. After halftime, UNLV surrendered a scoring drive of 52 yards, followed up by fumbling the ensuing kickoff. The offense has run a slower tempo recently and will likely do so here to keep the defense fresh, but this stop unit will have to be rock-solid in order to see UNLV compete with NDSU. This game has North Dakota State listed as a 3.5-point road favorite with a total set at 48.5. This total has been bet down from 51.5 on the opener. I agree with the move and feel this matchup is one between even teams. I'm willing to take NDSU's team total under 25.5. This game will be played at a very slow pace, and the Bison will operate very slowly when they have the ball. While this offense has put up a decent amount of points this season, the strength of schedule disparity in this matchup is monumental. North Dakota State has feasted on weak defenses, including Sac State , Fordham and Air Force . The Rebs have controlled the line of scrimmage this season and have done well to prevent explosives on the ground. NDSU won't find the chunk plays on the ground in this game, and I wouldn't be surprised to see UNLV get the Bison off the field early in this game until they settle in. The Rebels have given up some explosiveness through the air, something NDSU is ill-equipped to exploit in this matchup. UNLV has an excellent red-zone defense that has allowed just eight touchdowns on 17 attempts. I look for the UNLV stop unit to bow up in the red area and force NDSU to settle for field goals, something we've seen in recent weeks. The Rebels will run the ball a decent amount, and while they'll be effective, they won't be explosive. NDSU has made a concerted effort defensively to keep everything in front of it, and the defense forces long, methodical drives. UNLV's performance in the red zone has been terrible this season, as only 53% of trips have resulted in touchdowns, and the Rebs gamble on fourth-and-goal a lot. Doing that again will leave NDSU with long fields, so the Bison will take time off the clock on long, methodical drives. I think this game will be a lower-scoring competitive grind, with the winning team not surpassing 24 total points. This is a tough trip against a team that has played a much tougher schedule to date, so I will bet that the Bison offense struggles for the first time this season. Pick: North Dakota State Team Total Under 25.5

picks.headline: Bold Predictions for Georgia-Alabama Showdown
picks.blurb: Bold Predictions for Georgia-Alabama Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Alabama Crimson Tide and the Georgia Bulldogs will face off on Saturday and are going to have to weather both the storm of each other and Hurricane Isaias. As always, this matchup brings memorable moments. It brings drama. It brings instant-classics. I have to find a way to get bold with it. I lost out on all three of my bold predictions for the Vanderbilt game after hitting on one against Oklahoma. Fortunately, I have seen this movie plenty of times. Here are three bold takes for the game between Kirby Smart’s Dawgs and Kalen DeBoer’s Crimson Tide that I think can legitimately happen. 5 Total Turnovers Between Both Teams The ground will be wet, the wind will be hard and the rain will be coming down. The weather is projected to calm down for actual gametime, but now tabbed as Hurricane Isaias is going to make its mark all the way up the state of Alabama. You know what that means: sloppy football. We already saw the Georgia Bulldogs struggle with fumbles during the rainy Western Kentucky game in the second week. I suspect that could be an issue again if the weather truly is complicated. Alabama’s quarterback Keelon Russell, as good as he is, has not faced a defensive unit as talented or as violent as Georgia’s. He has been pretty clean this year, throwing only two interceptions and losing only one fumble to this point, but I predict he turns the ball over at least once himself. I would probably predict that even without the weather. Turnovers happen when these two teams face off. The weather will induce more of them. I am predicting five will come true. Gunner Stockton Scores Two Touchdowns on the Ground Georgia’s redshirt senior quarterback has yet to score a touchdown with his legs this season – something he did 10 times in 2025, leading the Dawgs in that category. I think he will do it twice on Saturday night. Stockton has not carried the ball near as much this season as he did at this point a year ago. He exploded for almost 100 yards on the ground at Arkansas thanks to a career-long 62-yard run. Georgia also hasn’t played in a big game yet. Stockton’s legs were a favorite in their important matchups a season ago. The danger comes in the red zone for opposing defenses. He had a red zone rushing touchdown against Tennessee. He ran two in against Kentucky. He scored the dagger with his legs against both Texas and Auburn. He ran one in from 22 yards out against Ole Miss in the regular season and then ran for two scores against the Rebels in the Sugar Bowl. I think Stockton will find the end zone again, and I think it will happen twice. It is the piece of Georgia’s red zone offense - which is extremely multiple - that hasn’t been dished out yet this season. Nate Frazier has his first 100-Yard Game of the Season Especially because of the potentially awful weather, I think Georgia is going to run the football a ton. Nate Frazier has gotten his rest since getting dinged up against Arkansas. He was off to a super hot start that has been slowed down due to him virtually missing 2.5 games. Chauncey Bowens has been ruled out for this game due to a foot injury he suffered last weekend. Even with the emergence and explosiveness of Dwight Phillips Jr., Frazier will likely see the bulk of the touches out of the backfield. Georgia operates a committee-style running back room, and Smart keeps saying that Georgia will continue to spread the football around. Frazier is still the lead back, and he will have his touches increased in big games. Loading recommendations... Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban is one of the analysts, alongside Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, Kirk Herbstreit and host Rece Davis. So, which panelists picked Alabama over Georgia, and how many chose the Bulldogs over the Crimson Tide? Note: Davis, the host, doesn't make picks, and the same is said for Herbstreit, who is on the call tonight. Prop pick #2: Gunner Stockton Over 199.5 passing yards Georgia hasn't leaned heavily on its passing game early this season, with just 44.53% of its plays coming through the air. In the other two games, the Bulldogs largely had things wrapped up by halftime, eliminating the need to air it out or prompting them to bring in the backup. This matchup should require Stockton to play all four quarters, and with the spread suggesting Georgia could be playing from behind, the senior QB may need to air it out. And for those SPRINTING to @ me on X about the weather, The Weather Channel forecasts the storm to pass by kickoff, with just a 24% chance of precipitation and winds of 7-9 mph. Georgia is fresh off a smackdown on Vanderbilt, 38-14, while Alabama dismantled Mississippi State 56-23. This has game of the year potential, and there's been a lot of them in the SEC already! Georgia has the No. 1 rated offense and defense per PFF, averages the most points in the country, and allow the third-fewest rushing yards per game (57.4) — and all of that will be put to the test against Alabama. The Bulldogs pitched a second-half shutout against Vanderbilt and won 38-14 after leading 21-14 at the half. Georgia has allowed 20 or fewer points in all five games and 44 points over the last three games against Arkansas, Oklahoma, and Vanderbilt. The offense put up 471 total yards of offense, doubled Vanderbilt's first downs (26-13), and held the Commodores to 85 rushing yards. Alabama is coming off arguably their most impressive performance of the season. The Tide destroyed Mississippi State, 56-23, never trailing in the game. Alabama outgained Mississippi State in yards 483-302, went 6-of-9 on third downs, and forced four turnovers (2 INT, 2 Fumbles). Keelon Russell had another dominant outing with 301 total yards and four touchdowns (3 pass, 1 rush). Russell is climbing the Heisman Trophy rankings and a win over Georgia would likely jolt him to the top spot. Alabama has owned the series against Georgia winning 10 of the past 12, but the Bulldogs won the previous matchup 28-7. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Georgia vs Alabama Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Time: 7:30 PM Eastern Site: Bryant-Denny Stadium City: Tuscaloosa, AL TV/Streaming: ABC Game Odds for Georgia vs Alabama The latest odds as of Tuesday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Georgia Bulldogs (+102), Alabama Crimson Tide (-122) Spread: Alabama -1.5 (-112) Total: 52.5 points #2 Georgia Bulldogs Head Coach: Kirby Smart 2026 Record: 5-0 (3-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 51.4 PPG (1st) Defensive Points Per Game: 13.4 (12th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 97th 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 20th The Georgia Bulldogs Offense: Georgia is the highest scoring offense in the country which is odd because in years past, Kirby Smart has taken is foot off the gas against early season opponents. Georgia's scored 45, 41, and 38 points against SEC opponents so far with 471, 464, and 306 total yards of offense. Georgia ranks sixth in third-down offense (54.9%), fifth in passing efficiency (188.72), and 13th in turnover margin per game (+1.2). picks.headline: College Football 27 sim predicts winner, score of Georgia vs. Alabama
picks.blurb: College Football 27 sim predicts winner, score of Georgia vs. Alabama - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Bills stun Rams in OT WNBA Finals arena debacle Brewers beat Dodgers again Guardians win ALCS Game 1 College Football 27 sim predicts winner, score of Georgia vs. Alabama Georgia Bulldogs running back Nate Frazier (3) runs against the Alabama Crimson Tide Owen Hillman, UGA Wire Fri, October 9, 2026 at 8:34 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Georgia Bulldogs (5-0, 3-0 in SEC) face their biggest test of the season against the Alabama Crimson Tide (5-0, 3-0 in SEC). Both teams have looked like national championship contenders; inclement weather concerns persist, and Kirby Smart's record against Alabama isn't very promising. Georgia has had strong wins against everyone they've faced, winning by at least 20 against every opponent (Tennessee State, Western Kentucky, Arkansas, Oklahoma, Vanderbilt). However, Alabama has played a tougher schedule, with Eastern Carolina and Florida State as their non-conference opponents so far, and has won against now-ranked Kentucky, South Carolina, and formerly ranked Mississippi State. There's a lot of pressure for the Bulldogs to keep rolling, and considering the state of the SEC, this could decide a contestant in the SEC championship too. Georgia vs. Alabama College Football 27 simulation Result This sim was conducted with the idea that Isiah Canion, Josh Ford, and Jorden Edmonds would be out. They were all listed as questionable on the injury report. Neither team got on the board in the first quarter due to the field conditions. It wasn't until the second quarter that the Crimson Tide struck first, with Daniel Hill rushing in a touchdown from 19 yards out to make it 7-0 at 9:44. Both teams exchanged punts, then on Georgia's next drive, Peyton Woodring nailed a 39-yard field goal to make it 7-3 at 2:50. Then, 40 seconds later, Keelon Russell's pass was intercepted by Justin Williams, who ran it back 19 yards for a touchdown to give Georgia a 10-7 halftime lead. Alabama countered with a Conor Talty 40-yard field goal at 8:33 to knot it up at 10, but then Georgia went on a long drive, capped off with a Nate Frazier touchdown to make it 17-10 with 3:22 left. Conor Talty kicked another field goal, this time from 37 yards out, to make it 17-13 by 8:13 in the fourth quarter, but Gunner Stockton fired a 73-yard bomb to Sacovie White-Helton for a touchdown to make it 24-13 Georgia. Nate Frazier essentially iced the game, as he ran in his second touchdown of the day from nine yards out to make it 31-13 by 3:33 in the fourth quarter. Alabama would get a garbage-time touchdown with Keelon Russell completing a screen pass to Kaleb Edwards to reach the final score of 31-20. Alabama got one more try, but Raylen Wilson picked off Keelon Russell again on the final play. It wasn't the most glamorous win for Georgia, but they got the job done. Both Georgia and Alabama had 4.5 yards per play, and Alabama did better on third down (eight for 16) than Georgia (five for 14). However, Georgia won the turnover battle, picking off Keelon Russell twice, while the running game did the rest. Gunner Stockton was uninspiring, going 17 for 25 for 161 yards and a touchdown and no interceptions. However, Nate Frazier came through on his return, with 95 yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries. The trenches helped Georgia win too. Georgia's offensive line did allow three sacks against Alabama, all by Jah-Marien Latham, but the Bulldog defensive line sacked Russell seven times, including three by Elijah Griffin and three by Josh Horton. Georgia would be 6-0 and in contention for the No. 1 seed if this were to hold in real life. Georgia would cover, considering they were 1.5-point underdogs against Alabama, and the under would hit by half a point. That would be an acceptable result for Georgia fans. The sim is 4-0 in predicting matchups, so hopefully this holds up too. This article originally appeared on UGA Wire: College Football 27 sim predicts winner, score of Georgia vs. Alabama

picks.headline: ‘They haven't seen anything quite like what Alabama has' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Alabama vs Georgia
picks.blurb: ‘They haven't seen anything quite like what Alabama has' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Alabama vs Georgia - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Bills stun Rams in OT WNBA Finals arena debacle Brewers beat Dodgers again Guardians win ALCS Game 1 Gary Cosby Jr.-Tuscaloosa News Zach Ragan Tue, October 6, 2026 at 5:03 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Alabama Crimson Tide and the Georgia Bulldogs will meet in Tuscaloosa on Saturday night. Georgia hasn't won a game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa since 2007. The Bulldogs will be looking to end that streak this weekend when they play on the road against the Crimson Tide. Both teams enter the game with a 5-0 record. The winner will instantly be one of the favorites to be the top overall seed in the College Football Playoff later this year. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Georgia vs Alabama ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Crimson Tide quarterback, made his prediction for the game and he thinks the outcome will be decided by just three points. McElroy has Alabama leaving Bryant-Denny Stadium with a 31-28 win. "Alabama has 13 takeaways this year," said McElroy on Tuesday . "That's top two in the sport. (Georgia QB) Gunner Stockton has thrown one interception all season, so something's got to give here. If Alabama can steal one or maybe two possessions, then that gives them a significant edge in a game that is very much a toss-up. I'm taking the Crimson Tide 31, Georgia 28. "On paper, Georgia has the much better defense. They give up less than four yards per play. That's the best in college football. But right now, they haven't seen anything quite like what Alabama has offensively. (Alabama QB) Keelon Russell is playing the best football of anybody on the entire field, and Georgia's going to have to blitz, I think, to get home before he lets it go. Kirby Smart is 90-3 in his career when Georgia scores 30 or more, and we've got the Bulldogs stopping just short of that. He's also 2-7 against Alabama and 120-14 against everybody else. So it's going to be very hard to take the Bulldogs against a really improved Alabama football team in Tuscaloosa. "I also think Alabama will force a takeaway or two that will ultimately be the difference in what is a three-point game. Look, Georgia brings the better defense to Bryant-Denny on Saturday night, but I think Alabama has the edge in just about everything else. Give me the Tide, 31-28." Georgia and Alabama are set to kick off at 6:30 PM CT/7:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ABC. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. The Saturday, Oct. 10 matchup marks the seventh time the former Oklahoma coach, Riley, will face the ex-Iowa State leader, Campbell. But it'll be the first time they meet in the Big Ten. Riley owns the upper hand in the head-to-head matchups against Campbell's Cyclone teams, going 4-2 all-time against him and ISU. But Riley already knows what to expect from a Campbell-led team . Oregon blocked out the noise and won in double overtime to prevent a Penn State home win. And the Ducks turned to a silent count on offense to withstand the noise. Perhaps USC rolls with something similar in this showdown. But Riley's past success against Campbell, plus USC showing signs of resurgence on defense, should be enough to avoid the upset. picks.headline: College GameDay makes picks for USC vs. Penn State whiteout
picks.blurb: The No. 19 USC Trojans enter Saturday night’s clash against the Penn State Nittany Lions at Beaver Stadium with their College Football Playoff hopes on the line. The Trojans will play in one of their most hostile environments this season: the Nittany Lions' annual whiteout game at Beaver Stadium, which is in primetime on NBC , with kickoff scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT. The Trojans are currently the underdogs, despite the Nittany Lions suffering two straight losses to the Wisconsin Badgers and the Northwestern Wildcats. DraftKings Sportsbook lists the Trojans as 1.5-point underdogs against the Nittany Lions. That didn’t stop a majority of ESPN’s College GameDay crew from picking the Trojans to beat the Nittany Lions as a road underdog. Here’s a look at the GameDay crew’s picks. ESPN College GameDay Predictions Desmond Howard: USC Nick Saban: USC Pat McAfee: Penn State Bryce Young (guest picker): USC Kirk Herbstreit: USC Can USC Pull Off a Statement Road Win Over Penn State? Despite being underdogs and struggling on the road under coach Lincoln Riley, USC’s offense has been among the Big Ten's best this season. Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava, who is in his second season as USC’s full-time starter, enters Saturday night’s matchup against the Nittany Lions as the Big Ten’s leading passer with 1,744 yards, 15 touchdowns, and three interceptions. Two of those three interceptions came in the Trojans' last two games against the No. 13 Oregon Ducks and Washington Huskies, which could be a concern for USC’s offense against the Nittany Lions, as one turnover could be costly in a game like Saturday night’s with Penn State. The Trojans are also depleted at wide receiver, which has always been a strength of their offense under Riley. The latest season-ending injuries to Corey Simms and Terrell Anderson are crushing blows to the Trojans' offense that will affect them in Saturday night’s game against USC. A pair of freshmen, wide receiver Trent Mosley and tight end Mark Bowman, are also listed as questionable for the primetime matchup against the Nittany Lions. Their potential absence will be yet another crushing blow for the Trojans' offense. Facing such a hostile environment on Saturday night against the Nittany Lions, it’s crucial the Trojans start fast and avoid mistakes early on in the game. In their 25-21 home win over the Washington Huskies at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Week 5, the Trojans offense got off to a slow start and even trailed by 11 early in the third quarter, before scoring 15 unanswered points to win. This is something the Trojans can’t afford to let happen on Saturday night when they face the Nittany Lions at Beaver Stadium. USC looks for its first win over Penn State as a member of the Big Ten, as the two last met in 2024 in Los Angeles, a game the Nittany Lions won 33-30 in overtime. A tough loss to Oregon was okay, but the wheels came off with six straight defeats, leading to an overhaul of the program. There's no need to fully panic quite yet, but after collapsing against Wisconsin in a 24-20 loss, and being run over by Northwestern by 21, this is a must-win moment with a trip to Michigan up next. USC got over its loss to Oregon with a great win over Washington, but there's a problem. If a road date at Penn State is your easiest game in the next month … USC vs Penn State: Quick Hits USC is starting a run of three road games in four, getting a week off before going to Wisconsin. Then it hosts Ohio State and then goes to Indiana . Penn State alternates road and home games until mid-November, going to Michigan next before getting a week off to get ready for Purdue. Penn State won 33-30 in the last meeting in 2024. USC won the two meetings before that in the 2009 and 2017 Rose Bowls. Temple was able to run for over five yards per carry in its 27-9 loss to Penn State, and Wisconsin managed to average just over four yards per pop in its win. And then Northwestern and offensive coordinator Chip Kelly found something that worked, running the ball 55 times for 413 yards and four touchdowns. USC will try to win with the short passing game – Northwestern's Aidan Chiles completed 71% of his passes last week – but if it commits to the run with well over 30 carries, it'll work. Why Penn State Will Win USC doesn't generate enough pressure from its defensive front, and that gives mobile quarterbacks plenty of chances to hit the midrange passes on the move. Penn State's Rocco Becht might not be devastating when he runs, but the offense is deadly when he's connecting. Defensively, chalk up the Northwestern game to a bad day. The Nittany Lion defense is great on third downs, and it's third in the nation in pass defense. However … USC vs Penn State Prediction, Betting Lines Penn State hasn't seen a passing game like USC's. The Trojan defense is shaky, and it has to prove it can hold up on the road after having issues against Rutgers a few weeks ago, but Jayden Maiava and the Trojan passing attack will be strong throughout. But USC won't run well enough. Embarrassed by the Northwestern game, Penn State comes out roaring and holds up through a fun four-quarter fight. picks.blurb: Final score predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game vs. USC - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Bills stun Rams in OT WNBA Finals arena debacle Brewers beat Dodgers again Guardians win ALCS Game 1 Final score predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game vs. USC Kevin McGuire, Paul White and Christopher Sheppard, Nittany Lions Wire Fri, October 9, 2026 at 12:03 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Enthusiasm for the Penn State whiteout game may have fizzled out in recent weeks after Penn State jumped out to an 0-2 record in Big Ten play after last week's debacle against Northwestern, but a primetime game in the national spotlight could be the perfect time for Penn State to reignite the season. Penn State hosts USC on Saturday night as the Trojans make their first visit to Beaver Stadium since 1994 and for the first time as a Big Ten opponent. The Trojans bring a dangerous offense to the game but are faced with some concerns about the defense. Can Penn State find its offense against the Trojans and pull off a big win against a ranked opponent in the whiteout game? Here are our final score and player of the game predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game against USC, along with some brief thoughts on the matchup. Kevin McGuire, Lead Writer The last couple of weeks have set off some serious alarms for me about Penn State, and that does not fill me with a great amount of confidence in the Nittany Lions going into this matchup against USC. The Trojans have struggled with the defense this season but I'm not seeing the firepower necessary to keep things too competitive with the Trojans on Saturdya night. After Northwestern ran all over Penn State's defense, I think the Trojans would be smart to try mimicking that with King Miller setting the tone on the ground and allowing Jayden Maiava to do his thing with the passing game. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt of USC will be a problem all nigth for the Penn State defense. Final score prediction: USC 27, Penn State 20 Player of the game pick: Jayden Maiava, USC quarterback Paul White, Contributor This hurts to predict, but I just don't see a way Penn State wins this game. The offense should be able to get back on track against a weaker defense, but if we couldn't stop Northwestern's offense, then I'm terrified to see what USC does. Final score prediction: USC 38, Penn State 27 Player of the game pick: Chase Sowell, Penn State wide receiver Christopher Sheppard, Contributor It feels like the gig is up for the Nittany Lions. What should be a celebration of one of college football's greatest modern traditions could turn into a State College massacre. I don't think that there will be much resistance from the blue and white, but I could see young edge talent Yvan Kemajou flashing some potential. (Photo by Randy Litzinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jared Slanina Thu, October 8, 2026 at 11:07 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Nittany Lions seek their first win in Big Ten play after stumbling to an 0-2 start. in conference play. Penn State (3-2, 0-2) vs. USC (5-1, 2-1) Kickoff: 7:30 p.m., Beaver Stadium, State College, PA The Betting Line: Penn State -1.5 (Fanduel) TV: NBC, 7:30 p.m., Noah Eagle (play-by-play), Todd Blackledge (analyst), Kathryn Tappen (sideline) Weather: A cloudy day with a high of 67, with temps dropping into the upper 50s during the evening. Matt Campbell: PENN STATE RECORD: 3-2, 1st Year OVERALL RECORD: 110-72, 15th Year Lincoln Riley: USC RECORD: 40-19, 5th Year OVERALL RECORD: 95-29, 9th Year VS. PENN STATE: 0-1 Tony Rojas is the only active player with more than 21 career TFLs and six career interceptions…Saturday will be the 19th full stadium white out in Beaver Stadium history…USC and Penn State are both in the top 10 in program wins and winning percentage…USC leads the all-time series 6-5 over Penn State…the two programs will be meeting for the second time as members of the Big Ten. Jayden Maiava is one of the best quarterbacks in the nation when he heats up. The likely future first round draft pick has continually improved in three years as a starter, and is enjoying his best season up to this point. He is completing 69% of his passes with 15 touchdowns and three interceptions, and is on pace to set career highs in just about every category. Maiava has accomplished this without wide receiver Trent Mosely, who was quickly establishing himself as one of the nation's best receivers as a true freshman. He has been out with an injury since week two, and is not likely to return on Saturday. The Trojans still have their typical number of playmakers at the skill positions. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, a freshman with the body of a veteran NFL receiver, has become the primary targets with 25 catches for 372 yards and three scores. Zacharyus Williams, another big-bodied receiver, has been a dangerous deep threat and is coming off his best game. Maiva also looks to tight end Mark Bowman often, a freshman who has become more involved with the offense in recent weeks – although he is questionable with an undisclosed injury. King Miller returns to the USC offense after rushing for just under 1,000 yards as a true freshman. He came back bigger and faster, and can be hard to take down at 6-0, 225 lbs. He can also be dangerous in the open field despite his size, and has a run of at least 20 yards in each of the past four games. Waymond Jones is another big, physical back who excels in short yardage situations. Penn State's defense appeared to be the strength of the team, and one of the best in the Big Ten. However, that sentiment was erased by Northwestern on Friday in of the poorest defensive performances in recent memory. The Wildcats put up 406 rushing yards, averaging 7.5 yards with each carry. Northwestern was able to run so freely that they only had 14 passing attempts while controlling the clock. It doesn't help that they will be facing a coach in Lincoln Riley that excels at creating offensive gameplans, and was just handed a blueprint for how to move the ball on the defense. It's hard to find any current point of optimism for the Penn State offense. The tackles have been unable to set the edge. The interior line is unable to open up running lanes or keep the pocket clean. The running backs have failed to find explosive plays, or provide a consistent ground game. Tight end Andrew Rapplyea and center Brock Riker are both playing through injuries that are obviously limiting their play. The receivers have shown promise, but don't get many chances because of all the off-target passes and balls regularly getting knocked down at the line of scrimmage. Rocco Becht has not yet shown he is capable of moving the ball against a Big Ten defense through two games. Despite being the nation's most experienced quarterback, he has often looked lost within the offense once the level of competition improved. Fortunately for Penn State, they are facing a defense that has been struggling after a positive start in non-conference play. The Trojans are ranked 14th or worse in the Big Ten in scoring defense, pass defense, total defense, and explosive plays allowed. USC gave up 30 points against Louisiana, 35 against Rutgers and 41 to Oregon in consecutive weeks. They are coming off a better result against a Washington offense decimated by injuries, holding them to 21 points and a key stop in the final minute to preserve the victory over the Huskies. If Penn State can find some rhythm, it may be against this defense. Safety Christian Pike is USC's most productive player, and should be on an NFL roster next season. He leads the team with 35 tackles, and has an interception and two pass breakups. Similar to Penn State, USC has a pass rush by committee and do not seem to have a dominate pass rusher who regularly makes plays in the backfield. Penn State fans will also recognize a couple of former Nittany Lions who transferred to USC over the off-season in linebacker Ta'Mere Robinson and defensive end Zuriah Fisher. SPECIAL TEAMS USC kicker Caden Chittenden is 6-of-7 on the season, with a career-long of 52 yards in 2024 while playing at UNLV. Punter Lachlan Carrigan is as consistent as they come, and has an average of 49.3 yards per punt. Penn State kicker Ryan Barker missed his second field goal of the season on Friday after not missing a single field goal that was not blocked in 2025. Barker has a career high of 49 yards, which he has hit on multiple occasions. Punter Nathan Tiyce is averaging 41.6 yards per punt this season, and is coming off a shaky performance against Northwestern with several short kicks. USC-27, Penn State-17 Maybe Penn State is able to prove they are better than the team we've watched in the last two weeks. Maybe there are some quick fixes to set things right. But for now, it appears the Nittany Lions are lost and searching for answers that may never come. It could be this team just isn't good enough to beat a quality opponent. Penn State will likely come out fighting and be boosted by the White Out crowd. However, my prediction comes to one simple fact – USC's offense can move the ball. Penn State still hasn't proven they can do so.

picks.blurb: Penn State football prediction, Matt Campbell vs USC in White Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Bills stun Rams in OT WNBA Finals arena debacle Brewers beat Dodgers again Guardians win ALCS Game 1 Story by York Daily Record Penn State football prediction, Matt Campbell vs USC in White Out Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This roughed-up Penn State football defense may face its toughest challenge yet on Saturday, Oct. 10, in Beaver Stadium . This group, and how well it recovers and responds, may well decide this critical night against the Top 20 USC Trojans , − the first White Out under coach Matt Campbell . Of course, the Nittany Lion defense was crushed last week at Northwestern , those 413 rushing yards allowed the fourth-most in school history. Now it must overcome one of the most dynamic attacks in the country. PSU podcast: Our Penn State football podcast with Devon Still, the White Out vs USC USC and star quarterback Jayden Maiava are averaging 311 passing yards per game, 467 yards overall. They move the ball up and down the field as well as anyone. And PSU defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn knows it intimately. He coordinated the Trojans ' defense under head coach Lincoln Riley the past two years before coming back to Penn State. He coached against Riley when he led UCLA's defense in 2023. "He's tough because he doesn't really have a playbook. You know, he just has plays. He's going to do what his guys do best," Lynn said this week about Riley. "He probably has the best scheme-beaters in the country. "There's times when he'll present things and it's like, 'Man, you just don't have an answer for it.'" Penn State defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn talks to reporters during football media day in Holuba Hall, Friday, August 7, 2026, in State College. Penn State football vs. USC prediction Expect Rocco Becht and the Penn State offense to look improved Saturday night. Becht has rescued himself from struggles in the past, and he'll be working against a suspect, inconsistent USC resistance that's been prone to game-changing lapses. But this night will truly turn on the PSU defense. It must find a way to not only hold the line of scrimmage but to upgrade its tackling pursuit and execution. If it cannot stop USC's power tailbacks it doesn't have much of a shot to slow down Maiava, either, no matter how good its secondary may be. And that would make life too conquer, everywhere else. These cornerbacks and safeties will be truly tested hard for the first time this season. The Trojans pass game features six receivers with 11 or more catches each, led by Kayden Dixon-Wyatt (25 receptions, 14.9 yard average, 3 TDs). A key will be whether the Penn State defense can deliver enough disrupting pressure on Maiava, particularly through its blitz packages. The big concern is that the Lions' edge rushers have rarely gotten to the quarterback so far, no matter the opponent. The Lions' run game, with its awkward four-man rotation, will be in the spotlight, as well. It must produce, at least enough to give its defense a break and keep USC and Maiava off the field as long as possible. Will Quinton Martin Jr. finally earn first-team carries again? A sidenote: Trojans' defensive end Zuriah Fisher, who transferred from PSU last winter, has six tackles and a sack so far. This Week 6 contest heading into the season was considered a pivotal game for the Nittany Lions (3-2, 0-2 Big Ten) as it was expected for them to be in a good spot after Week 5. While that ended up not being the case, they still have an opportunity to upset the Trojans and pull off a statement White Out win at home. Ahead of the matchup, both teams released their injury reports.
